problem.title: Preventing ThreadLocal Leaks in Worker Pools
problem.prompt: A Spring Boot / Tomcat service running 200 long-lived HTTP worker threads stores a `RequestContext` (containing a 256 KB parsed JWT/permission payload and user ID) in a `private static final ThreadLocal<RequestContext> CTX = new ThreadLocal<>()`. Over 48 hours of uptime, old-gen heap climbs steadily to 92%, GC pauses spike to 1.8 seconds, and intermittent bug reports show User B occasionally seeing User A's permissions when an upstream auth filter throws an exception before overwriting `CTX`. Diagnose both the memory leak and the cross-tenant security bug, and design a leak-proof context propagation mechanism.

spark.summary: `ThreadLocal` keys are `WeakReference`s, but their values are strongly referenced inside `ThreadLocalMap.Entry` for as long as the pooled worker thread lives—leaking megabytes of request/tenant state and causing cross-request data corruption.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, always clear `ThreadLocal`s in a deterministic `finally` filter/interceptor, avoid storing large buffers or classloader-bound objects in `ThreadLocal`, and migrate to Java 21+ `ScopedValue` where possible.

_nextProblem.title: Mitigating TLS Handshake Storms on Reconnects
_nextProblem.prompt: Your Envoy ingress fleet (40 pods, 4 vCPU each) terminates 120,000 persistent mTLS/TLS 1.3 connections from 1,500 internal microservice pods. When an NLB target group or Envoy EDS/CDS reload resets connections simultaneously, all 1,500 pods immediately reconnect at ~60,000 handshakes/sec. Because TLS session tickets are disabled (`disable_stateless_session_resumption: true`) and leaf certs use RSA-2048, Envoy CPU pins at 100%, handshake latency hits 8 seconds, client timeouts trigger new reconnects, and the cluster enters a permanent handshake storm. Design a storm-proof TLS termination and reconnection architecture.
